title: The word between number and noun
summary: Count with a measure word using the pattern number plus measure word plus noun.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: Chinese does not say 三书 sān shū for three books. Between the number and the noun stands a measure word, written 量词 liàngcí, so you say 三本书 sān běn shū. The pattern is number + measure word + noun, and with 这 zhè (this) or 那 nà (that) the number 一 yī usually disappears: 这本书 zhè běn shū, 那杯咖啡 nà bēi kāfēi. The measure word itself never disappears. The same slot carries questions too: 几个人 jǐ gè rén? (how many people?), 哪本书 nǎ běn shū? (which book?), 几张票 jǐ zhāng piào? (how many tickets?).

A handful do most of the work: 个 gè for people and many objects, 本 běn for bound things (一本书 yì běn shū, 两本杂志 liǎng běn zázhì), 张 zhāng for flat things (一张纸 yì zhāng zhǐ, 三张票 sān zhāng piào), 条 tiáo for long and flexible things (一条鱼 yì tiáo yú, 那条路 nà tiáo lù), 只 zhī for animals (一只猫 yì zhī māo), 位 wèi as the polite people word (三位客人 sān wèi kèrén), 双 shuāng for pairs (一双鞋 yì shuāng xié), 辆 liàng for vehicles (两辆车 liǎng liàng chē), 杯 bēi for drinks (两杯水 liǎng bēi shuǐ), and 件 jiàn for matters and garments (一件事情 yí jiàn shìqing). If you are unsure, 个 gè is understood far more often than a wrong special word, but learn each noun with its own measure word as one chunk.

body.speaker: A
body.en: How many oranges would you like?

body.speaker: A
body.py: zhè shuāng xié nǐ yào ma?
body.en: Do you want this pair of shoes?

body.speaker: B
body.py: bú yào. qǐng gěi wǒ liǎng píng shuǐ.
body.en: No. Please give me two bottles of water.

blocks.title: Practise these
body: 请给我三张纸。 qǐng gěi wǒ sān zhāng zhǐ. — Please give me three sheets of paper.
我弟弟养了一只猫。 wǒ dìdi yǎng le yì zhī māo. — My younger brother keeps a cat.
门口停了四辆车。 ménkǒu tíng le sì liàng chē. — Four cars are parked at the door.
这里有三条路。 zhèlǐ yǒu sān tiáo lù. — There are three roads here.
我们每人要一杯水。 wǒmen měi rén yào yì bēi shuǐ. — Each of us wants a glass of water.
你买了几本书？ nǐ mǎi le jǐ běn shū? — How many books did you buy?

blocks.body: Independent, unofficial practice material written from scratch for general learners of Mandarin. It teaches measure words, and nothing in it is taken from, copied from, or aligned to any commercial course, textbook brand, app, or official exam. It is not an answer key for any test.
